cause_en: Incorrect results can be assigned for an autocancelled and rescheduled test A correct result is obtained for the rescheduled test while no results are obtained for the auto cancelled one The interpretation of the rescheduled test is shown in the results detail screen and traceability report However the system shows a wrong result interpretation in the results screen and this result is sent to the LIS The issue occurs due to a very rare concurrency problem in the database management Three conditions must be met to trigger the incident A test is automatically cancelled and rescheduled This test is rescheduled while its status is already RUNNING The software is not able to successfully discard the cancelled test Due to this error the test remains internally linked to two different instances of the technique the cancelled one and the one that is created upon rescheduling The microtube results from the cancelled execution have no information but the software assigns a default interpretation result The information contained in the executed instance is correct However the interpretation result shown in the results screen for this technique is from the cancelled technique instance
corrective_action: If you have installed software version 4.5.0, you are requested to install patch v4.5.1 on your Erytra analyzer, which is already available and can be remotely installed, or to install software version v4.6.1, which will be available for installation in the next weeks. If you have installed software version 4.6.0, you are requested to install software version 4.6.1 on your Erytra analyzer, which will be available for installation in the next weeks.

cause_en: A malfunction has been identified with the DI analyzer relating to slide identification DI has a shuttle which transports slides from the Sysmex CF into the DI for analysis and back to the Sysmex CF after analysis The shuttle has a fetch position for slides coming into the DI for analysis and a return position for slides going out from the DI after analysis At the occasion when the barcode reader reads the incoming slide the incoming and the outgoing slides are located next to each other in the shuttle If the analyzer fails to read the barcode of the incoming slide there is a risk that it instead reads the barcode of the outgoing slide The incoming slide is thus assigned the same identifier as the outgoing slide This malfunction may lead to misattribution of patient results Potential clinical impact includes incorrect or delayed diagnosis initiation of inappropriate treatment or delay in necessary treatment any of which could result in serious health consequences depending on the patient condition and test type Although no adverse health outcomes have been confirmed to date the malfunction represents a potential for serious indirect harm
corrective_action: A malfunction has been identified with the DI-60 analyzer relating to slide identification. DI-60 has a shuttle which transports slides from the Sysmex CF into the DI-60 for analysis, and back to the Sysmex CF after analysis. The shuttle has a fetch position (for slides coming into the DI-60 for analysis) and a return position (for slides going out from the DI-60 after analysis). At the occasion when the barcode reader reads the incoming slide, the incoming and the outgoing slides are located next to each other in the shuttle. If the analyzer fails to read the barcode of the incoming slide there is a risk that it instead reads the barcode of the outgoing slide. The incoming slide is thus assigned the same identifier as the outgoing slide. This malfunction may lead to misattribution of patient results. Potential clinical impact includes incorrect or delayed diagnosis, initiation of inappropriate treatment, or delay in necessary treatment, any of which could result in serious health consequences depending on the patient condition and test type. Although no adverse health outcomes have been confirmed to date, the malfunction represents a potential for serious indirect harm. For this reason, a Field Safety Corrective Action (FSCA) is being initiated to mitigate the risk and ensure continued patient safety. Internal investigation has confirmed that the malfunction is caused by conditions in the CCU firmware in combination with newer barcode readers (Honeywell Vuquest and Jadak FM-5). Specifically, the barcode reader has a field of view that is too large, allowing capture of the barcode on the return slide (located next to the fetch slide). The barcode reader continues to attempt barcode reading after the gripper has released the return slide, thereby exposing its barcode. To eliminate the root causes, corrective actions have been implemented in the CCU firmware (version 4.2.7), which includes: - Reducing the effective field of view of the barcode reader. - Preventing additional barcode reading attempts once the gripper has released the return slide. Firmware version 4.2.7 has already been introduced in manufacturing. As part of this FSCA, all affected DI-60 instruments in the field will be updated with the corrected firmware via Distributor's service engineers. Distributors are required to confirm completion of the update. These actions are justified to prevent recurrence of the malfunction, to mitigate the risk of slide misidentification, and to ensure patient safety. 1. Action To Be Taken by the User ☒ Identify Device ☒ On-site device modification / inspection The following actions shall be taken by the user of the device: 1. Identify whether any of your DI-60 analyzer(s) are affected by verifying the serial number(s) against the list of affected units provided in Table 1. 2. If your unit(s) are affected, please implement the following interim measure to mitigate the risk of sample misattribution: a. Before signing each order, confirm that the number of slides in the order matches the number of slides ordered. No order shall contain more slides than prescribed. b. Await contact from Sysmex service personnel, who will arrange installation of the updated CCU firmware. 3. You may continue to use the system(s) in accordance with its intended use, provided the above instructions are followed 4. Please ensure that this Field Safety Notice is circulated to all users of the device so that they are made aware of the potential issue. 5. Retain this letter until the firmware correction has been implemented. Ensure that the notice is kept in a visible and accessible location. 6. Fill in the customer response form and send via e-mail to whomever you received the FSN from

cause_en: Medtronic has identified an internal manufacturing issue with the Small Diameter Stapling Reload s Cover Tube Press step which can produce parts with a malformed press This press in the external cover tube creates an interference hold of internal components within the stapling reload s shaft which enables adequate transfer of force through the reload to fire the stapler and maintain jaw orientation during firing A malformed cover tube press can lead to internal components movement during firing leading to the potential for uncontrolled motion The issue can occur using either the Endo GIA Ultra Universal Stapler or Signia Stapling System While using Endo GIA Ultra Universal Stapler or Signia Stapling System uncontrolled articulation in either direction can occur during firing as well as after firing if the user continues to squeeze the handle or press the fire button after the firing of the reload has been completed Uncontrolled articulation is also possible if the reload is being used outside of the indicated tissue thickness range Update October Medtronic has identified an internal manufacturing issue with the Small Diameter Stapling Reload s Cover Tube Press step which can produce parts with a malformed press The tube press on the reloads were measured and found to be out of specification Engineering functionally tested one device and found that the reload de articulated during firing Production and releases were suspended The malformed cover tube press occurred from an incorrect parameter setting for long cover tube assembly in the Programmable Logic Controller PLC program for mm CFNs Parameters were reviewed for the mm PLC program and found to be correct The parameter for mm was validated to be mm for long cover tubes however a line of code in the logic allowed for this parameter to be reverted to the previously validated setting of mm Although a similar line of code exists for short cover tubes there are additional aspects to this line of code that prevented it from being activated The scope of this issue has been bounded to all long cover tube lots built since the implementation of the new parameters under CDP totaling four lots N F Y N F Y N D UY N B UY
corrective_action: • Identify and quarantine all unused impacted product listed above. • See Attachment A for guidance on identifying affected lots. • Return all quarantined devices to Medtronic. Please contact your Medtronic Representative in case you need assistance with the return of the affected devices. o Credit for the returned affected devices will be issued based on the RGA number. o If purchased from a distributor, contact your distributor directly to arrange for the return of the devices back to your distributor. • Pass on this notice to all those who need to be aware within your organization or to any organization where the listed affected lots may have been transferred or distributed.

cause_en: BD was made aware via customer complaints that dropping the Alaris Pump Module may cause damage to internal components that may not be apparent or readily visible More specifically drops or severe jarring may damage the Alaris Pump module bezel assembly which provides the mechanical foundation for critical pumping components This damage can cause under infusion over infusion unregulated flow or failure of the Alaris Pump module to calibrate Please note that this issue is separate from worldwide field action MMS FA of Alaris Pump Modules LVP for units built and service kits manufactured with FR resin FR between April and June
corrective_action: Clinical User Actions 1. Customers should NOT USE a device that has been dropped or severely jarred. Devices that have been dropped or severely jarred should be segregated and sent to biomedical engineering for inspection, as directed in the BD Alaris™ System with Guardrails™ Suite MX User Manual: “If a device or accessory is dropped or severely jarred, take the device out of use immediately. Send the device to biomedical engineering for inspection to ensure the device is functioning properly before reuse.” 2. Prior to use, inspect the Alaris™ Pump Module for visual damage. If the device has physical damage, remove from service and send to biomedical engineering for further inspection and testing, as directed in the BD Alaris™ Infusion System User Manual: “To ensure that the BD Alaris™ Infusion System remains in good operating condition, visually inspect the system before each use. Check all visible surfaces and moving parts on the devices. If you observe damage in any way or find the device does not function as expected, return it to biomedical engineering for repair.” Biomedical User Actions 1. Perform the testing as specified in the Level of Testing Guidelines in your Technical Service Manual for a dropped device, including rate accuracy verification testing. If any test fails, perform the applicable steps in the troubleshooting section of your Technical Service Manual, which may include replacement of the pumping mechanism. See Technical Service Manual Section. 2. Continue to perform annual preventive maintenance, including rate accuracy verification (as discussed in the previous action item), on all of your Alaris™ Pump modules, as specified in the Alaris System Maintenance Guide. Preventive maintenance is important in ensuring regular testing of any potentially dropped or damaged device that was not immediately removed from use. BD Actions: 1. BD is providing a Tip Sheet (Appendix A) to be distributed to all clinical users, environmental services staff, transport staff, biomedical engineering and any other key personnel who may handle Alaris™ Pump Modules. The Tip Sheet is intended to remind all personnel who handle the Alaris™ Pump Modules that dropped/damaged units should be removed from service and inspected. 2. BD will be adding reinforcements to applicable labeling to reiterate that if devices are dropped or severely jarred, they should be removed from service and inspected. These warnings currently exist in your Alaris™ System with Guardrails™ Suite MX User Manual. 3. BD continues to investigate long-term product enhancements related to this issue. cause_en: BD was made aware via customer complaints that dropping the Alaris Pump Module may cause damage to internal components that may not be apparent or readily visible More specifically drops or severe jarring may damage the Alaris Pump module bezel assembly which provides the mechanical foundation for critical pumping components This damage can cause under infusion over infusion unregulated flow or failure of the Alaris Pump module to calibrate Please note that this issue is separate from worldwide field action MMS FA of Alaris Pump Modules LVP for units built and service kits manufactured with FR resin FR between April and June
corrective_action: Clinical User Actions 1. Customers should NOT USE a device that has been dropped or severely jarred. Devices that have been dropped or severely jarred should be segregated and sent to biomedical engineering for inspection, as directed in the BD Alaris™ System with Guardrails™ Suite MX User Manual: “If a device or accessory is dropped or severely jarred, take the device out of use immediately. Send the device to biomedical engineering for inspection to ensure the device is functioning properly before reuse.” 2. Prior to use, inspect the Alaris™ Pump Module for visual damage. If the device has physical damage, remove from service and send to biomedical engineering for further inspection and testing, as directed in the BD Alaris™ Infusion System User Manual: “To ensure that the BD Alaris™ Infusion System remains in good operating condition, visually inspect the system before each use. Check all visible surfaces and moving parts on the devices. If you observe damage in any way or find the device does not function as expected, return it to biomedical engineering for repair.” Biomedical User Actions 1. Perform the testing as specified in the Level of Testing Guidelines in your Technical Service Manual for a dropped device, including rate accuracy verification testing. If any test fails, perform the applicable steps in the troubleshooting section of your Technical Service Manual, which may include replacement of the pumping mechanism. See Technical Service Manual Section. 2. Continue to perform annual preventive maintenance, including rate accuracy verification (as discussed in the previous action item), on all of your Alaris™ Pump modules, as specified in the Alaris System Maintenance Guide. cause_en: To assess the regulatory impact of the release of software version of BIO FLASH P N

The installation process now includes a validation step to ensure the application is only installed on the supported operating system version. 2. Cybersecurity Enhancements a. Increased password complexity requirements. b. User accounts are temporarily locked for 5 minutes after multiple failed login attempts. 3. Logging Improvements a. Added a button to print the Instrument Log. b. Enhanced logging performance: logs are now written in parallel during active runs, improving overall system responsiveness. 4. Specimen Lifetime Configuration a. The Specimen Lifetime setting (in hours) defines how long a specimen remains in the database after its first entry. b. Acceptable values range from 0 to 999 hours (default: 6 hours). A value of 0 means the specimen is never removed. 5. Cartridge Compatibility: added support for 200-test cartridges (availability to be confirmed). 6. Results Screen Optimization a. Added "Expand" option in the submenu for Results and Results Archive. b. Replaced results archiving with a pagination feature. c. Improved automatic results printing functionality. d. Enhanced sorting options in the results list report (e.g., by barcode, assay). e. Improved results filtering capabilities. 7. Performance Optimization: general application performance improvements, enabling safe operation with large panels and high result volumes. 8. User Interface Updates: updated the System Cleaning Solution wizard completion message. 9. LIS Demographics Handling: a. Optional display and storage of demographic data received from the LIS. b. cause_en: An event was reported by a Medtronic field representative that during routine defibrillation threshold testing at an EV ICD implant Ventricular fibrillation VF detection was appropriately met and the capacitors were charged to deliver a shock however following charge end the device was no longer showing sense markers and therapy was aborted The Medtronic representative stated that it was difficult to tell if the device lost sensing telemetry or other interaction Sensing resumed after seconds and redetection occurred but an external defibrillation shock was manually delivered to convert the rhythm prior to fulfilling device confirmation and therapy delivery A second induction attempt through the device resulted in a shock being delivered after charge end that successfully terminated the arrhythmia Medtronic internal review of the device data determined that the absence of sensing markers occurred due to a firmware timing interaction between the charge end and a ventricular sense VS event coincident with a drop in device measured R wave amplitudes When an EV ICD detects a ventricular arrhythmia and determines therapy is required the device charges the capacitors and delivers the shock If the end of the capacitor charge interrupts an in progress R wave amplitude measurement there is a potential for the dynamic sensing algorithm to remain at its first plateau of of the prior R wave measurement amplitude This may be impactful and lead to a delay in high voltage therapy if the amplitudes decrease at the time of the interrupt The root cause of the delayed therapy was determined to be VF undersensing due to a firmware timing interaction with the charge end event and a VS event coincident with a significant decrease in the amplitude of the VF signals that was not large enough to be sensed at the initial automatic sensing threshold The sensitivity remained at the initial automatic sensing threshold of of the prior sensed event amplitude without automatic adjustment due to charge end CE interrupting an in progress amplitude measurement When the amplitude of the subsequent signal falls below this sensing threshold as seen in the reported complaints delayed tachyarrhythmia therapy may result This happens because a non committed shock cannot reconfirm and sync to a ventricular sensed beat Non committed shocks include all cardioversion CV therapies in the ventricular tachycardia VT and fast ventricular tachycardia FVT zones as well as the first shock in the ventricular fibrillation VF zone Syncing to an R wave to deliver a shock is standard practice for transvenous ICDs and external defibrillators and is not unique to EV ICD This particular automatic sensing threshold issue is unique and isolated to EV ICD due to sensing thresholds being controlled by firmware Sensing behavior is defined in hardware for transvenous ICDs
corrective_action: Kindly refer to the letter

device: NextSeq 550Dx High Output Reagent Kit v2.5 (75 cycles)
cause_en: Illumina has received several customer complaints describing leak events in NextSeq Dx sequencers where liquid was found under the flow cells Based on field feedback received the leaks were intermittent occurrences at the start middle and end of the sequencing runs After an investigation Illumina determined that this issue was due to loose debris found on flow cells gaskets received from the third party supplier of the flow cells The quality issue was related to a change of the third party supplier s manufacturing site The products impacted are the flow cells components of the NextSeq Dx sequencing reagents kits which are class A In vitro Diagnostic Medical device IVD intended for sequencing of DNA libraries on the NextSeq Dx Instrument
corrective_action: Illumina Actions We have completed a root cause investigation and implemented preventative action to prevent further recurrence. All impacted products in our inventory have been identified and contained. Illumina has notified the pertinent local and international regulatory bodies, including the Competent Authorities, of this issue. Required Customer Actions If you received reagent lots listed in the Appendix, dispose of these reagents per local regulations. See the NextSeq 550Dx Instrument Reference Guide for additional instructions on proper disposal. Please ensure proper personal protective equipment (PPE) is utilized including, but not limited to, eye protection, gloves, and a laboratory coat. If you have or suspect you have come in contact - directly or indirectly via skin or aerosol - with the reagents in the flow cell, please follow your laboratory's standard safety and first aid procedures immediately. Please complete the Verification Form to acknowledge that you have carried out the Required Customer Actions above. We kindly ask that you e-mail the completed form to Illumina Technical Support within 5 business days. Alternatively, you may call or e-mail Illumina Technical Support to provide the information requested on the form.

cause_en: Cepheid has become aware of a rare genetic mutation event between Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Neisseria meningitidis that caused some Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains to lack target sites for the Cepheid Xpert CT NG test leading to false negative results
corrective_action: Cepheid recommends that laboratories and clinics using the Xpert® CT/NG test as their molecular method for the detection of N. gonorrhoeae monitor for decreases in the positivity rate and ensure that discordant laboratory results (e.g. testing negative on the Xpert® CT/NG test but positive for NG by culture/microscopy or testing negative on Xpert® CT/NG test but positive for NG using anther NAAT be investigated further and reported to Cepheid. Cepheid also asks that you acknowledge receipt of this Urgent Field Safety Notice by completing the attached Customer Response Form and either emailing the completed form to CFQ@cepheid.com or faxing it to +1 (408) 716-3143. Cepheid will not send a reply or confirmation of received response forms.

cause_en: Philips IntelliVue Patient Monitors provide a feature for pausing all alarms for a configured timeframe or for switching all alarms off for an infinite period until they are switched back on by the user The infinite Alarms Off feature is an important functionality in specific clinical environments such as the Operating Room Cath lab or during resuscitations to reduce the audible alarms which may present unnecessary distractions during closely monitored procedures or interventions Philips has received complaints that the IntelliVue monitors did not alarm In some cases these complaints alleged delayed patient treatment due to the monitors not alarming and in some cases there were reports of severe patient harm or death It was determined that in these instances the Alarms had been switched off for an infinite period and the user may have been unaware that the alarms were off
corrective_action: Philips is informing customers of the observed errors and related hazards of enabling infinite Alarms Off, including providing instructions on how to configure the device alarm settings. Philips recommends reviewing the configuration of the monitors with infinite Alarms Off functionality enabled and reconfigure settings to require additional confirmation to ensure users are aware of their action when activating infinite Alarms Off. For IntelliVue MP5 models only: Philips is developing a software update which will enforce the additional confirmation step when the user enables infinite Alarms Off. To update your MP5 software to include this feature, please reach out to your local Philips representative. Philips is also providing an educational video on this topic. Scan the QR code or visit learn.philips.com to access the educational video on how to configure and use the infinite alarms feature in the Philips Learning Center (PLC). Enter your PLC username and password or create an account and then enter this enrollment key to access the video:

cause_en: Philips has identified that during maintenance activities excessive bending forces may be applied to the ethernet cable connector transmitting image data from the detector to the system This may cause the cable to be pulled out of the connector s strain relief potentially leading to intermittent disconnections between the internal wires and the connector pins If one of the connecting pins loses connection live X ray image will no longer be displayed and the error message Doselink Error X ray aborted will be shown on the user interface In some instances a restart of the C arm stand may temporarily resolve the issue

cause_en: Description of the product problem BD is pleased to announce that we have resumed production of a modified version of the BD BACTEC MGIT PZA Kit which includes modified inoculation methods and reduced shelf life BD has conducted a thorough review of the performance from all supported inoculum sources using the synthetic raw material and the following change has been implemented for the BD BACTEC MGIT PZA Kit Only inoculum prepared from MGIT tubes days post positivity can be currently supported Inoculum prepared from MGIT tubes days past instrument positivity are currently not supported Inoculum prepared from solid media are currently not supported Additionally the shelf life of the product has been adjusted from months to months to reflect the latest internal supporting data
corrective_action: BD Actions: 1. BD will continue to work with global regulatory authorities to reintroduce BD BACTEC™ MGIT™ 960 PZA Kit. BD will resume receiving and fulfilling customer orders for this product in markets where permitted, based upon regulatory requirements while maintaining ongoing quality improvements and performance monitoring. 2. BD continues to investigate long-term solutions and will actively work with global regulatory authorities to reintroduce the BD BACTEC™ MGIT™ 960 PZA Kit with the original claims. To date, BD does not plan to initiate any further advice or information in a follow-up FSN. cause_en: The purpose of this letter is to share information regarding the Model Symmetry VNS Therapy Generator which is designed to deliver Vagus Nerve Stimulation for chronic or recurrent depression As of September LivaNova has received two reports indicating that the battery status may temporarily display a full battery level i e indicator when a range would be expected Importantly this behavior does not affect the delivery of VNS Therapy The generator will accurately deliver therapy as programmed and the overall longevity of the generator battery is unaffected The reported impact has been limited to user dissatisfaction with the battery status display There have been no reports of patient harm and therapy delivery remains unaffected The generator battery longevity is unaffected by this issue All clinically actionable battery indicators low battery indicators such as Intensified Follow up Indicator IFI Near End of Service NEOS and End of Service EOS are accurately presented The temporary fluctuation does not interfere with the clinical use and will self correct i e resolve prior to display of the IFI NEOS and EOS indicators The Model battery status indicator may Inaccurately show depletion at an accelerated rate involving the and battery indicators early in product life Fluctuate and temporarily display full generator battery status i e indicator when a range would be expected This issue presents in the middle of product life As a reminder product labeling recommends the following actions for the lower battery indicators and importantly each of these indicators is accurately presented by Model Remaining i e indicator Battery level is within normal operating range and no action is required Intensified Follow up Indicator IFI Battery has depleted to a level where more frequent clinical monitoring is recommended Near End of Service NEOS Generator should be replaced as soon as possible End of Service EOS Generator is no longer supplying stimulation and immediate replacement is recommended If the generator is not replaced it will eventually lose the ability to communicate with the software This behavior is limited to Model generators listed in Attachment of this letter No other VNS Therapy generator models are affected

cause_en: The Instructions for Use IFU ZDOCK for the devices listed above contains the instruction The chest tube can now be secured to the skin by using the fixation device R PG FX or suture or both and is ready for connection to a suitable sealed drainage system such as the Rocket Blue Bottle or Rocket Ambulatory Bag The fixation device mentioned is no longer supplied by Rocket Medical and Rocket Medical determines that securing the device by suture is a mandatory action to prevent risk of disconnection
corrective_action: The IFU has been updated to include revised guidance regarding the need for a suture, in steps 14 and 15. The updated text now states: "The chest tube must now be secured to the skin by suture and is ready for connection to a suitable sealed drainage system such as the Rocket Blue Bottle or Rocket Ambulatory Bag. Further support to the catheter can be provided by the fixation device." Customers will be contacted to inform them of the update to the instructions and provided with an updated IFU.

The notice informs users of the specific product and version numbers affected by the issue, and any work around that can be used to avoid the issue. (If applicable)  Sites affected will be all digital Linear Accelerators (Synergy, Infinity, Versa HD, Elekta Evo) up to and including SN 157644, Harmony & Harmony Pro up to and including SN 451054. A copy of the Important Field Safety Notice is to be kept with the most current labelling and all personnel working with the product should be made aware of the content of the letter. The customers are instructed to complete and return the Important Field Safety Notice Acknowledgement form to their local Elekta representative as soon as possible but no later than 30 days from receipt. Elekta will release an Important Field Safety Modification (IFSM) to identify potentially faulty discharge rod crimping and provide further instructions. The modification will include procedures for verifying the reliability of the discharge rod crimping and replacing affected components. The target date for release is March 2026.

corrective_action: • Discontinue use and dispose all Bicarbonate OSR6x37/OSR6x90 lots listed in Table A in the IMPACT section of this letter, following your laboratory protocols and local regulations. Contact your local Beckman Coulter representative for replacement or re-imbursement. • For Bicarbonate OSR6x37/OSR6x90 lots listed in Table B in the IMPACT section, if elevated LDH levels are suspected, please assess results in conjunction with patient’s LDH values. • Share the content of this letter with your laboratory and/or Medical Director to evaluate the requirement for a retrospective review of Bicarbonate results for neonatal patients and patients with elevated LDH levels.

cause_en: Using Xpert BCR ABL Ultra test kits with specimens that have markedly elevated white blood cell count cells L may potentially cause inaccurate results
corrective_action: Cepheid recommends that laboratories and clinical facilities utilizing the Xpert® BCR-ABL Ultra assay for quantification of BCR::ABL1 and ABL1 mRNA transcript levels in peripheral blood specimens from t(9;22)-positive chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) patients undergoing tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy, assess white blood cell count (WBCC) prior to testing in cases where elevated white blood cell count is suspected. Specifically, if the WBCC exceeds 30,000 cells/μL, the specimen should be processed in accordance with the “Retest Procedure for ERROR (Code 2008) or INVALID (Type 2)” as detailed in the “Retests” section of the IFU for the following scenarios: - Cases where INVALID test results are observed and are associated with an elevated WBCC. - Cases of valid results in which an elevated WBCC has been observed. This recommendation is intended to mitigate the possibility that viscous samples could yield a falsely low or false negative result.

corrective_action: 1. Please note the true use-by dates for the impacted lots that are provided in Table 1 above. generation is not available When this occurs the system does not show any message to the user indicating that X ray generation is not possible A warm restart may resolve the situation in some cases A cold restart will always resolve the situation Issue Loss of X ray after Phase Fault Philips Azurion systems are designed to automatically recover from phase faults being an abnormal condition in which one or more phase voltages drop to near zero When a phase fault occurs the X ray generator software initiates an automatic recovery process to restore full system functionality during which imaging X ray functionality is not available for approximately seconds Due to a software issue during this recovery the communication with the system software may be lost resulting in the system not recognizing that the generator has recovered and is ready for operation In this situation the system shows the user message Generator is busy starting up no X ray possible If the phase fault is detected by the generator during acquisition the system also shows the message Run Aborted Tube Problem A cold restart of the system will always restore system functionality Issue Missing live X ray on the FlexVision monitor When viewing high resolution images i e resolution above x pixels visible on screen as Live K the FlexVision monitor may not display the X ray live window blank screen when one of the following specific sequence of actions is followed a Changing the live viewset up by maximizing another view on the FlexVision monitor or by explicitly removing the Live X ray application from the screen or hiding it only possible if X ray is disabled or by activating the screensaver or by starting comfort Themes followed by a warm restart of the system b Performing a warm restart to the system and then changing the FlexVision screen layout from applications to less than applications A warm restart will resolve the issue However the issue will re occur if the sequence of actions described in scenario a or b are again performed A cold restart will resolve this issue unless afterwards a warm restart is performed for any reason in combination with the sequence of actions described in scenario a or b Issue System keeps restarting When the Patient database in the Azurion system s Suite PC which stores metadata about patients studies procedures and series objects contains more than series objects system functionality becomes unavailable To address this the Azurion system initiates a recovery restart However because the number of series objects remains unchanged the issue persists causing the system to repeatedly perform recovery restarts No message is displayed to indicate this situation To resolve this issue a reinstallation of the Suite PC software is required Issue AMC triple drive Due to a firmware issue in the Advanced Motion Controller AMC Axis drive integrated electronic and mechanical component responsible for the precise movement and positioning of the Azurion s stand a Movements of the stand might be slow when this occurs the message Adjustment of frontal stand is required is displayed to the user When this occurs D scan functionality is not available The message Rotational scanning is unavailable Reselect the X ray protocol is displayed to the user To resolve this issue a calibration of the system by service is required b Motorized movements of the stand might become unavailable when this occurs the message Adjustment of frontal stand is required is shown to the user A cold restart of the system may temporarily resolve the issue in some cases Manual movements of the stand remain available Table movements are not impacted by this issue Issue C Partition of Suite PC running out of free space The C drive of the Azurion Suite PC may gradually lose available space due to the accumulation of printer spool files The Windows operating system creates a spool file for each print job and deletes it once the job is completed successfully If a print job fails these spool files are not removed and accumulate after each system re start when the Windows operating system retries the print job consuming disk space When the system re starts and the C drive is full motorized movements are disabled The following messages appear on the screen Some geometry movements are not available and The geometry is starting Do not change SID Issue System remains in continuous restart mode after the start up Due to a software issue the License Manager which verifies installed licenses and enables optional functionality in the Azurion system based on the available licenses expands the Windows registry database at every system start or restart Over time the registry may grow beyond the maximum size that the License Manager can load When this happens the License Manager cannot start and the system will enter a continuous reboot loop The Azurion system will not complete booting and the message X ray system is booting remains displayed on the screen Issue Misalignment of Marker Tool Overlay Applicable only to Azurion systems with the Marker Tool option The Marker Tool allows clinical users to draw freehand markers on a previously acquired X ray image to add guidance or indicate a region of interest Markers are displayed on all images within the series and on any images acquired after they are created When geometry movement exceeds predefined thresholds e g angulation or rotation differences greater than or a Beam IsoCenter to Patient deviation greater than mm markers are hidden When the geometry returns within the threshold markers reappear However they may not be restored to their exact original position and can deviate by several millimeters If the Marker Tool is used during a clinical procedure to indicate the correct placement of a device this deviation could lead to incorrect placement of the device Issue Longitudinal Position Error Applicable only to Azurion systems with Poly G frontal stand When requesting a movement of the frontal stand in longitudinal direction the Azurion system may detect a mismatch between the expected longitudinal set position and the measured actual position of the stand This mismatch is caused by a glitch in the longitudinal position value provided by the position sensing potentiometer When the mismatch is detected the motion power to the frontal stand is automatically cut off The message Some stand movements are not available is displayed to the user In this situation X ray imaging and table movements will continue to function This issue can be resolved with a cold restart of the system or by restarting the geometry

cause_en: The manufacturer has received reports in which the Display Module of the corpuls system has unexpectedly shut down and initiated an automatic reboot during patient care This results in a temporary interruption of certain device functions typically lasting between to seconds with an average duration of seconds This limited reboot is triggered by the device s internal software safety mechanisms as part of its fault management strategy The function is designed to preserve core functionality and maintain operational safety Importantly this does not represent a full system reboot once the Display Module restarts the device continues to operate as intended without the need for user intervention
corrective_action: As part of our post-market surveillance and risk control process, we are implementing a product correction by releasing an enhanced software version, REL 4.4.2, which addresses the root cause of the self-initiated safety reboot mechanism.

cause_en: The Vanta A Clinician Programmer CP App v and v will display a System Error if the user selects the Start Usage button twice when interrogating a new implantable neurostimulator INS This error prompts the user to restart the CP app and contact Medtronic for assistance Upon subsequent interrogation of the INS the Vanta A CP App will display a Validation Error prompting the user to resolve the error in order to proceed with the INS interrogation If the Validation Error is not resolved the user is unable to complete the first attempt at interrogating the INS This issue does not occur with other Medtronic neurostimulators Based on the investigation it is found that the issue was caused when the user selects the Start Usage button twice when interrogating a new INS The Validation Error that displays prevents the user from completing first attempt at interrogating the INS if not resolved This issue presents at the point of use Updating the Vanta A CP App to or later addresses the issue as the telemetry dialog screen will transition directly into the next screen of the workflow which prevents the Start Usage button from being shown or selected a second time

cause_en: under specific conditions the lift s electromagnetic holding force may disengage unexpectedly allowing unintended downward movement of the lift This event may occur during the procedure described in the TS Instructions for Use IFU Chapter Removing a rack or foreign object from the carry in line
corrective_action: Actions to be taken by the customer: To prevent injury, never place your hands around the lift section at any time. In addition, please follow these instructions when handling rack jams or similar errors: ✓ Pay special attention not to insert your hands around the lift section during any intervention. ✓ If a rack, tube, or any object becomes lodged around the lift section, tum off the power. After confirming that the lift section has moved to the bottom dead point, carefully remove the rack and blood collection tubes. ✓ If the rack or blood collection tubes are jammed in the lift section and cannot be removed with one hand, contact Sysmex and request an FSR for assistance. Please ensure this notice is communicated to all relevant personnel and retained in a visible location until the software update is completed. Actions to be taken by Sysmex: Sysmex will implement a software update to improve lift position control to prevent unintended sudden drops of the lift section by ensuring that, after an error occurs, the lift automatically returns to the home position. Our service team will contact you to schedule the installation of software version 00-18 or later.

cause_en: Medtronic has determined that Vanta may be susceptible to not communicating with the clinician programmer and or the patient programmer system HH Handset and TM Communicator Although the INS can continue to deliver therapy to the patient within programmed parameters the inability to communicate can put the patient at risk In some instances if there is no communication with the INS during the implant procedure troubleshooting may delay the surgical procedure and may require a replacement INS In other instances if there is no communication with the INS post procedure it might not be possible to adjust therapy and may cause the patient to experience inadequate therapy i e return of underlying disease symptoms In rare instances if communication cannot be restored to the INS via a recommended mitigation an unanticipated surgical intervention may be needed to explant and replace the INS
corrective_action: • Please review your facility’s inventory of Vanta INS devices and take the following actions: • Identify Vanta INS devices manufactured with the old firmware by referencing the PIN number on the device packaging. PIN number 977006002H indicates the device has the old firmware. • Return unused affected product per the return instructions. • Complete the enclosed Customer Acknowledgement Form. When complete please return the form to Medtronic • This notice should be passed on to all those who need to be aware within your organization or to any organization where the potentially affected devices have been transferred. • Please maintain a copy of this notice in your records.

cause_en: Issue System remains in continuous restart mode after the start up Due to a software issue the License Manager which verifies installed licenses and enables optional functionality in the Azurion system based on the available licenses expands the Windows registry database at every system start or restart Over time the registry may grow beyond the maximum size that the License Manager can load When this happens the License Manager cannot start and the system will enter a continuous reboot loop The Azurion system will not complete booting and the message X ray system is booting remains displayed on the screen Issue Longitudinal Position Error Applicable only to Azurion systems with Poly G frontal stand When requesting a movement of the frontal stand in longitudinal direction the Azurion system may detect a mismatch between the expected longitudinal set position and the measured actual position of the stand This mismatch is caused by a glitch in the longitudinal position value provided by the position sensing potentiometer When the mismatch is detected the motion power to the frontal stand is automatically cut off The message Some stand movements are not available is displayed to the user In this situation X ray imaging and table movements will continue to function This issue can be resolved with a cold restart of the system or by restarting the geometry
corrective_action: Philips will address the identified issues by implementing software updates in all affected systems. Philips expects to have software update 3.1.5 (FCO72200635, FC072200671), that resolves issues 1, released by Q1 2026 (subject to regulatory clearance). The Longitudinal Position Error (issue 2) will not be resolved with software update 3.1.5. The solution for this issue is planned for Q4 2026 (subject to regulatory clearance) with software update 3.1.15 (FCO72200684).

cause_en: Certain Philips Allura Xper and Allura CV systems use a Laird cooling unit to control the flat detector s temperature This cooling unit is housed in a system cabinet in the technical room Philips has identified that a limited number of Allura Xper and Allura CV systems may lack a drip tray beneath the cooling unit This component is intended to prevent potential leaking coolant liquid from contacting electrical components If it is not installed there is a potential for coolant liquid to contact electrical components This could lead to electrical short circuits which may trigger system fuses and result in system shutdown Electrical short circuits could cause elevated temperatures in insulating materials which may result in smoke formation In severe cases deterioration of insulation could produce sparks and combined with flammable coolant liquid and high temperatures lead to fire
corrective_action: Philips will inspect the affected systems to confirm that the drip tray is installed and check if there are leakages. Your local Philips representative will contact you to schedule a visit for a Field Service Engineer to perform this activity. Philips expects to start this activity in February 2026.

cause_en: In rare instances the handle may detach from the syringe during use due to an insufficient amount of adhesive on the handle The lack of adhesive is not detectable prior to use In a single instance the detachment occurred concurrently with an adverse event
corrective_action: 1. Holding the cap and barrel together during use may effectively prevent detachment. 2. Visual indicators such as pressure drops on the gauge can alert users to potential failures. Refer to the product Instructions for Use. 3. Simulated use testing showed that handle separation results in flow restoration. 4. Should the handle detach during use and the balloon not completely deflate, pull the handle out of the inflation syringe, disconnect the inflation syringe from the catheter, and use an alternate syringe to generate vacuum and aspirate residual contrast.

corrective_action: When using the device, all instructions, including warnings and cautions contained in the Instructions for Use must be followed with heightened awareness. cause_en: During internal investigation Philips identified that the recent PIC iX software SW patch modifies Mobile Event Notification filter settings without providing any indication to the user when upgrading the system When patching a PIC iX X i e system that uses the default event filters for mobile notifications upgrading to overrides existing default filters and applies the new default filters for version The overridden filters can lead to the situation where alarms which were previously configured to distribute to mobile devices are no longer sent and no notification is provided by the system While all default event filters are overridden when patching to any customized configurations applied to high level filter categories subcategories or individual filters are maintained and migrated successfully
corrective_action: Philips representative will contact you to obtain PIC iX 4.5.1 SW patch for PIC iX systems running software version 4.5.0.

cause_en: GE HealthCare has become aware of a cybersecurity vulnerability affecting Centricity RIS i configured with Instant Messenger When Instant Messenger is installed and running a malicious actor could exploit this vulnerability to perform unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in Instant Messenger which could potentially impact system availability and or lead to ability to manipulate data Instant Messenger is an optional module which is not installed by default The vulnerability is not present in RIS i systems without Instant Messenger or where Instant Messenger has been disabled There have been no injuries or unauthorized access to patient data reported to GE HealthCare as a result of this issue
corrective_action: Customers with RIS-i Versions 4.2.24 thru 7.0 SP0 will get a Customer Letter, Instant Messenger will be de-installed, and Instant Messenger setup will be removed. Customers with RIS-i Versions 7.0 SP1 thru SP6 will get a Customer Letter and software upgrade.

cause_en: Sysmex has been made aware that in the above mentioned software versions when measuring XN CAL in Blood Bank BB mode the WBC value was approximately higher than expected Furthermore if calibration was performed using that XN CAL subsequent measurements of residual leukocytes in actual blood products or samples would be erroneously underestimated by about Our internal investigation revealed that an incorrect calculation had been incorporated into these software versions The false low result only occurs under specific conditions as below Software Version BB mode is activated Calibration performed in BB mode with one of the affected aforementioned SW versions i e if calibration of BB mode has been performed with any other software version this issue does not affect your device
corrective_action: Actions to be taken by the customer: Please check the version of the BB mode currently in use. If it is version 22.20-00 or version 22.21-00, you may continue using it without any issues. If you are using an affected version, please contact your Sysmex representative. Please confirm with your Sysmex representative whether calibration of the device has been performed in BB mode using one of the affected aforementioned software versions. If calibration was performed in BB mode, please either refrain from reporting WBC count from BB mode until the Sysmex representative completes the corrective action or continue while taking into account that the true residual white blood cell count may be approximately 15% higher than the reported value. Sysmex advises you to consult your facility's physician and/or pathologist to determine any clinical implications (including retrospective review and/or re-testing). Please ensure this notice is communicated to all relevant personnel and retained in a visible location until the software update is completed. Actions to be taken by Sysmex: The Sysmex representative will visit your site to perform immediate action, either by adjusting the relevant calibration factor to 15% higher or by changing the version to 22.20-00 or 22.21-00. Sysmex will develop and will provide you the permanent corrective action as soon as possible. Communication of this Field Safety Notice: Distribute this FSN to all responsible persons within your organization and return the Acknowledgement of Receipt (AoR) with your signature to your authorized local Sysmex representative.
